passages.original: 554, i Jul.) ab adolescentia sua devotus Deo esse cæpit, diligensque ex tota anima DOlnioum, et ea quæ Deo dilecta esse uoverat diligebat. Pater ejus nomine Georgius c, mater vero Leocadia a stirpe Vectii Epagati descendens, quem Lugduni passum Eusebii testatur Histo- ria, qui Ita de primoribus senatoribus fuerunt, ut in Galliis nihil inveniatur esse generosius atque nobi- lius. Cumque ei pater cujusdam senatoris fliam quærere vellet, ille assu'npto secum uno puerulo Inona- sterium Cromonense * expetiit, Sesto situm ab Arverna urbe milliario, suppłiciter abhatem exorans ut gibi comam capitis tondere dignarelus.
passages.english: (554, 1 July) from his youth began to be devoted to God, and loving the Lord with his whole soul, he loved those things which he had come to know were beloved by God. His father was named George, and his mother Leocadia, descended from the line of Vettius Epagathus, who, as the History of Eusebius testifies, suffered [martyrdom] at Lyon; and they were so much among the foremost senators that nothing is found in the Gauls more well-born and noble. And when his father wished to seek for him the daughter of a certain senator, he, taking one young servant with him, went to the monastery of Cournon, situated six miles from the city of Clermont, humbly begging the abbot that he would be pleased to cut the hair of his head for him.
passages.notes: The passage opens mid-sentence: the subject is Saint Gallus (see preceding context; '554, 1 Jul.' is an editorial date/feast note, apparently 'AA. SS.' or similar). Scanning errors corrected: 'DOlnioum' = Dominum, 'uoverat' read as noverat ('had come to know'), 'Ita' = ita, 'fliam' = filiam, 'assu'npto' = assumpto, 'Inona- sterium' = monasterium, 'Sesto' = sexto, 'gibi' = sibi, 'dignarelus' = dignaretur. Stray footnote marks ('c', '*') omitted. 'Cromonense' identified as Cournon near Clermont (Arverna urbs); 'Vectius Epagatus' is Vettius Epagathus, martyr of Lyon in Eusebius, Ecclesiastical History 5.1.
